correctness.rationale: Exact independent radial factorization Y=RZ for arbitrary full-dimensional centered convex bodies yields E[R^2]=d/(d+2), both covariance-normalized affine kernels and an explicit positive-part difference. The radial integral G_d is evaluated with the exact threshold d/(d+2), and G_d(s)>(s-1)_+ precisely above that threshold. The equality criterion therefore holds for all x and all d>=1. For K=-K, supporting functional normalization and covariance Cauchy-Schwarz imply u_x(-x)<=-1 at every boundary x. Full support of the radial cone law gives strictness there, and convexity puts the maximum of the boundary projector on the boundary. Both disk constants are independently integrated. check.py executed and passed 91 consistency assertions; finite quadrature corroborates and does not prove infinite claims.

originality.rationale: The strongest relevant published affine projector calculation gives exact norm and positivity loss only for a simplex under one measure; its result does not imply a cross-measure ordering. The inspected cone-volume research proves geometric concentration and stability, not affine reproducing-kernel inequalities. The inspected manifold L2-projector research provides boundedness under stable-basis hypotheses, not a comparison between volume and its radial pushforward on every convex body. Searches for radical mixtures, Lebesgue functions, covariance and cone-volume variants found no statement dominating the exact pointwise difference, equality criterion or symmetric-body strictness. Unidentified historical equivalences remain a risk; priority is not independently certified.
residual_risks: An equivalent theorem may exist using radial-mixture convex order terminology, projection constants or general positive-part kernel comparison not captured by available searches.

value.rationale: This solves a natural geometric sampling question for degree-one least-squares: how moving sampling from interior volume to its canonical cone-boundary law changes worst-case amplification. It gives an all-centered-body pointwise comparison with exact equality criterion and a strict all-symmetric-body operator-norm and positivity-loss ordering. A direct disk/interval gap illustrates quantitative consequences. This structural comparison is not a textbook kernel computation, an arbitrary slice or a known-table recomputation; it does not purport to solve higher-degree or unrelated boundary sampling.
